en: Although invisible, the air around us is made of gas molecules that have mass and take up physical space.
Melting solid ice into liquid water is a physical change because the water molecules themselves do not change their chemical identity.
When sugar dissolves in tea, it does not disappear; its molecules simply spread out evenly to form a uniform solution.
Rusting is a chemical change where solid iron reacts with oxygen in the air to form a new substance called iron oxide.
Liquid water can evaporate into a gas at room temperature, meaning evaporation does not require the water to reach its boiling point.
Mixing sand into water creates a mixture rather than a solution because the solid sand particles do not dissolve and will settle.
Honey flows much slower than water because it has a higher viscosity, which means its liquid molecules experience greater internal friction.
Burning a piece of wood is a chemical change because it transforms the original material into entirely new substances like ash and smoke.
A heavy steel ship floats because its hollow shape lowers its overall density below that of water, proving density determines buoyancy, not just weight.
The white mist above a boiling kettle is not a gas, but tiny liquid water droplets that condensed from cooling steam.
Unlike most liquids that shrink when freezing, liquid water expands and becomes less dense when it turns into solid ice.
If you boil saltwater until it completely evaporates, the solid salt will be left behind because the water turns to gas but the salt does not.
